item.content:encoded:
Riyadh airport attack: Two injured Indians remain in ICU, says Embassy Two injured Indians remain in the ICU following the October 10 Riyadh airport attack, with others recovering. The Indian Embassy advised nationals to stay indoors during aerial attacks, follow local rules, and note that flight suspensions and airport disruptions continue across Saudi Arabia. ANI | Updated: 16-10-2026 19:49 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 19:49 IST

Large plume of black smoke rises from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Two of the several Indian nationals injured during the October 10 attack targeting Riyadh airport continue to receive treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia stated on Friday. The update additionally noted that one further Indian citizen is in the High Dependency Unit (HDU), with three others recovering in a normal ward. The latest status update was communicated via a fresh advisory issued by the Embassy, which highlighted that Riyadh's international airport remains closed to flight operations. Meanwhile, airports in Dammam, Jeddah and Medina remain operational, though certain disruptions persist. Stating precautionary measures, the advisory noted, "In view of the prevailing situation, Indian nationals should continue following instructions by local authorities, stay indoors in case of an aerial attack, and refrain from filming, publishing or sharing any information, photos or videos related to the ongoing events." According to the Embassy, Indian carriers have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia. Specifically, Air India and Air India Express have suspended operations across all routes until October 20, whereas IndiGo has halted services until October 24. Furthermore, Akasa Air has suspended its flights to Riyadh until October 24 and to Jeddah until October 21. Conversely, Saudia maintains scheduled flight operations to Indian destinations from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. Meanwhile, Flynas operates scheduled flights along the Dammam-Lucknow sector, and Flyadeal has announced the introduction of Dammam-Mumbai flights scheduled for October 17-18. For Indian nationals seeking urgent departure, the Embassy suggested considering transit routes through Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar, subject to obtaining the requisite visas. Addressing prospective travellers, the advisory stated, "Indian nationals planning to travel to Saudi Arabia, including for Umrah, are advised to take into account the ongoing disruptions at Saudi airports and the possibility of flight cancellations, which may result in extended stays." Earlier on Thursday, India's Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Vipul, delivered a video message to the Indian community following the recent attacks, conveying India's condemnation of attacks on civilian facilities and infrastructure within the country. He mentioned that the Embassy had established dedicated helplines to assist Umrah pilgrims encountering difficulties, while cautioning individuals planning journeys to Saudi Arabia from India to account for potential disruptions. Ambassador Vipul stated, "In the current situation, all of us have to remain calm and alert. Especially in case of an aerial attack, we have to remain indoors," adding that distributing any photographs or videos concerning the attacks violated Saudi law and risked legal complications. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
China's central bank to further open up Chinese financial markets to foreigners China's central bank governor pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying yuan assets can meet the growing diversification needs of global investors. Reuters | Updated: 16-10-2026 14:22 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 14:22 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

China's central bank governor pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying yuan assets can meet the growing diversification needs of global investors. Pan Gongsheng noted rising geopolitical risks, profound changes in the global economic landscape and rapid advances in AI. "China’s steady economic growth, and rapid development of high-tech industries provide solid support for RMB assets," a People’s Bank of China (PBOC) statement quoted Pan as saying in a Thursday speech given on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. The PBOC will continue to expand risk management tools to expedite investment and financing, according to the statement. China has stepped up efforts to open its capital markets and to promote yuan internationalization, at a time when US President Donald Trump's trade war and unpredictable foreign policies dent trust in dollar assets. Global financial markets have also become more turbulent as investors increasingly worry about whether companies embarking on massive investment in AI will manage to make sufficient earnings gains amid higher borrowing costs. Pan said the PBOC will promote broader global acceptance and use of yuan bonds as eligible collateral, strengthen cross-border financial infrastructure connectivity and support the development of offshore yuan markets.

Magnitude 7.0 earthquake jolts Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula; no tsunami threat issued An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 on the Richter scale struck Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula region on Friday, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) and the National Center for Seismology (NCS). ANI | Updated: 16-10-2026 09:56 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 09:56 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 on the Richter scale struck Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula region on Friday, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) and the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said there was no tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat following the earthquake. According to the NCS, the earthquake occurred at 9:05 am IST today at a depth of 152 km, with its epicentre located at latitude 52.068° North and longitude 157.164° East. The EMSC reported a preliminary magnitude of 7.0, placing the earthquake approximately 123 km southwest of Vilyuchinsk in the Russian Federation. In a post on X, the EMSC said the earthquake had been confirmed by seismic data. Its data separately recorded the event at magnitude 6.9, with a depth of 130 km and coordinates of 52.059° North and 157.234° East. The EMSC placed the earthquake approximately 146 km south-southwest of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, a city with a population of around 187,000, and 80 km north-northeast of Ozernovskiy, which has a population of around 2,600. The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration recorded the earthquake at magnitude 7.0, with a depth of approximately 148 km, and located it around 415 miles southwest of Bering Island in the Komandorski Islands region. In its assessment, NOAA stated that there was no tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat. The earthquake's reported magnitude and depth varied slightly across monitoring agencies, with the EMSC recording a magnitude of 6.9 in its detailed data, while the NCS and NOAA reported a magnitude of 7.0. Further details on the impact of the earthquake are awaited. (ANI)
